notes: Both supplied 'Of's belong to אָשִׂיחָה: the first under rule 44, as the preposition by which the English verb reaches its bare object, and the second as that same morpheme's distributed occurrence over the coordinated member under rule 25. The competing reading treats them as rule 33 function words on the two bare nominals; it is named here under rule 8.
כְּבוֹד and נִפְלְאוֹת are rendered attributively ('glorious', 'wondrous') under rule 28, so the chain's single written 'of' falls to הוֹד as rectum under rule 19.
